title: Match Messaging Volume Measurement Flaw
scenario: BooedUp's product team is evaluating whether the recent Type Score model update improved engagement. The team wants to understand if users who Match are messaging each other more frequently.
prompt: A product manager proposes tracking 'Total messages sent after Match connections' as the key metric for the next sprint. The PM says this directly measures whether Matches are leading to more conversation. What is wrong with this metric as stated? Propose a corrected version.
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Example: 'Should be normalized per Match. Messages per Match is better.'
expected_themes: messages per Match is the correct form
reference_answer: Should be normalized per Match connection. Messages per Match is better.

grading_rubric.description: Answer explicitly states the metric is not normalized or is a raw count without a denominator

grading_rubric.criterion: Names Match connections as the normalization basis
grading_rubric.description: Answer proposes normalizing by Match count, Match pairs, or number of Matches
Answer suggests a rate form such as 'messages per Match' or 'avg messages per Match connection'

hints: Think about whether the metric can be compared across time periods with different Match volumes.
What would happen to this metric if Match volume doubled but engagement per Match stayed flat?
The flaw is about the missing denominator. What should you normalize by?
common_mistakes: Proposing 'messages per user' instead of 'messages per Match' — this mixes users who never Matched into the denominator
Suggesting median instead of mean — the problem is not outliers, it's the lack of normalization
Claiming the metric doesn't measure 'quality' — the issue is structural (no denominator), not conceptual
stakeholder_rationale: This counts all post-Match messages so we see if the Type Score update drives more conversation.

numerator.label: Messages sent after Match connection established
Total messages sent in the period

denominator.label: Match connections established in the period
Active users who initiated or accepted a Match
Total active users in the period
Users who sent at least one message

guardrail.label: Message response rate (replies per first message)
Time to first message after Match
